title: Feeding habits of the notothenioid fishes Patagonotothen sima (Richardson, 1845) and Patagonotothen cornucola (Richardson, 1844) along shallow waters of argentine patagonia
content:
Abstract

Information on the feeding ecology of intertidal notothenioid fishes remains limited in Argentine Patagonia, particularly for Patagonotothen sima. This study examined the diets of P. sima and P. cornucola and their spatial and seasonal variation using stomach-content analysis. Sampling was conducted at four coastal localities between March 2021 and March 2022. Patagonotothen sima was collected at two localities and P. cornucola at three; the interspecific comparison was restricted to Cerro Avanzado during winter. Patagonotothen sima fed mainly on polychaetes and small crustaceans, including tanaidaceans, amphipods and decapods, and exhibited an intermediate niche breadth (0.44). In P. cornucola, amphipods and polychaetes were important at Cerro Avanzado, whereas Exosphaeroma sp. and amphipods were prominent at Yamana. At El Pique, the diet was dominated by Exosphaeroma sp., with a narrow niche breadth (0.25), compared with intermediate values at Cerro Avanzado (0.56) and Yamana (0.59). Significant Site × Season interactions were detected in both species, as well as an interspecific difference at Cerro Avanzado during winter. These findings provide a detailed characterisation of the diet of P. sima in Argentine Patagonia and highlight spatial and seasonal variation in the trophic ecology of both species.
